response.markdown_report:
Select **endpoint-preserving temporal patching**: test whether earlier-context information changes predictions through an intermediate NextItNet state while keeping the terminal item fixed.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, frequency-matched old substitutions were less disruptive than random substitutions in Movies and CDs; their absolute effects remained negative. This indicates weaker measured sensitivity, without establishing harmful history. Second, readout-position restoration can copy an integrated representation. Earlier-position interventions offer narrower temporal localization but may miss distributed mediation. Third, exact host validation candidates remain unavailable. Diagnostic ranking changes cannot establish validation improvement.

**Insights from related work.** NextItNet provides depth and temporal intervention coordinates [1]; exact dependency sets must include gates, residual branches, masks and normalization. Corruption, metrics and patch windows affect localization [2]; endpoint-preserving permutations test conditional order sensitivity and may create unrealistic histories. Successful subspace patches can activate dormant pathways [3]; this finding neither invalidates nor certifies full-vector patches. Sampled metrics depend on candidate protocols [4], requiring explicit candidate counts and tie handling.

These insights define three directions: temporal specificity, intervention reliability and evaluation scope. Their conceptual map is:

| Axis | Existing probe | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input | Endpoint/order perturbations | Endpoint-preserving order contrast | Permutations may be unnatural |
| Mediator | Readout-position states | Earlier occupied state plus window controls | Distributed or redundant paths |
| Evidence | Diagnostic ranks/margins | Paired restoration/disruption, parity checks | Host validation benefit |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earlier-position bidirectional patching [1–3] | 5/7/6 | Adds temporal localization; reusable; existing hooks help | Established method; benefit uncertain; dependency/control work substantial |
| Two-site factorial patching [2,3] | 6/7/7 | Exposes nonadditivity; supports pathway studies; bounded grid | Scale-dependent; hybrid interpretation uncertain; more forwards |
| Candidate-draw stability audit [4] | 3/6/3 | Clarifies measurement sensitivity; broadly useful; simple scoring | Familiar; mechanisms unresolved; catalog costs grow |

At 20% progress, retain the first idea. Prespecify one intermediate residual boundary and an architecture-derived earlier-position rule before measuring effects. Preserve terminal ID, padding, candidates and original maximum-nonzero readout. Patch every eligible corruption in both directions, avoiding responsiveness-based selection. Report raw margin/rank changes; avoid unstable normalized recovery.

Bound execution to 32 uniquely identified training users/category, three permutations, two control users and 120 seconds/category, using seed 42. Verify hook counts, replacement values, identity patches and activation changes; compare local patches with coherent-window and whole-layer controls. Distinguish structural unreachability from null numerical effects. Record partial execution and missing controls explicitly.

Average permutations within users; report paired intervals, repeat/novel strata and coverage. Freeze selection rules and reserve confirmation users to limit diagnostic overfitting. Keep one checkpoint/category and pinned macro validation HR@10 selection unchanged.

References: [1] NextItNet; [2] Zhang & Nanda, 2024; [3] Makelov et al., 2024; [4] Krichene & Rendle, 2020. Links and limitations appear below.

idea.description: Extend the staged NextItNet diagnostic with endpoint-preserving, earlier-position bidirectional full-vector activation patching. Within each category’s single frozen model, perturb earlier ordering and intervene at one prespecified intermediate residual boundary and earlier occupied position whose audited dependencies connect edited inputs to the original final nonpadding readout. Measure all eligible corruptions and distinguish local intervention effects from coherent-window controls and distributed mediation.
idea.motivation: The supplied results show category-dependent training sensitivity, without establishing that older history should be removed. Current readout-position patches can copy an already integrated representation; earlier-position interventions test a narrower propagation hypothesis. However, one null patch cannot establish absent history processing, and successful restoration cannot identify a unique naturally used feature. At 20% research progress, this bounded extension remains preferable to a larger factorial search, provided implementation verification, candidate definitions and uncertainty are made reproducible.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions containing formulas, counts, exclusions, execution errors, numerical controls, missing reasons and protocol details. Preserve view.model as the actual trained module and all ModelView interfaces: item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Keep existing diagnostics and callable helpers; explicitly state which helpers run. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions. Unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits must remain unavailable.

Cache at most ten loader batches and retain at most 32 uniquely identified training users/category, one event each. Match each encoded prefix and aligned final positive to a unique training endpoint; exclude ambiguous matches with counts. Select by a deterministic seed-42 shuffle of eligible user IDs rather than observed margins, corruption responsiveness or patch success. Reserve the final eight selected users for confirmation; use the first 24 for exploration. Do not revise the fixed protocol after inspecting confirmation outcomes. This split limits within-probe adaptation but does not provide independent validation or remove prior search bias. Report actual split sizes and missing confirmation results.

Use evaluation mode and torch.inference_mode(); inference_mode does not set eval(). Preserve the original maximum nonzero readout index, never count-1. Exclude empty or non-left-padded sequences and invalid aligned targets. Audit FP32 features and score finiteness. Save and restore every submodule’s training flag, backend settings and relevant RNG states in finally, including cleanup after errors or timeout.

Reuse existing diagnostic candidate IDs when available and valid; otherwise create and record one explicitly diagnostic uniform-without-replacement candidate set per event using local seed 42. Include the aligned target exactly once, including repeat targets. Sample up to 99 unique nonreserved negatives excluding the target and all observed training-history items for that user. These are not host validation candidates. Freeze candidates across every condition. Report candidate IDs, actual counts, shortages and repeat-target prevalence. Define the primary ranking summaries on events with 99 negatives; report shorter sets separately because easier candidate sets change HR@10. With at most ten total candidates, HR@10 is guaranteed and must be labeled degenerate. Break exact score ties by ascending item ID, independent of target identity; report tie frequency. Rank is one plus the number of candidates with a higher score or an equal score and smaller item ID. Define margin as target score minus the maximum alternative score, rank change as patched minus recipient rank, and diagnostic hit as rank <=10. Missing alternatives make margin undefined.

Generate three independent seed-42 permutations of occupied positive-lag positions per user, leaving the endpoint, padding pattern, width and earlier-item multiset fixed. Record each permutation and changed position set. Retain identity permutations in coverage and all-draw summaries with explicitly zero input-intervention effects; label nonidentity summaries separately. Do not rejection-sample until an effect appears. These interventions test order sensitivity conditional on endpoint identity and may produce implausible sequences. A future natural-history matched-pair experiment is a separate estimand and should not be silently pooled with permutation results.

Before measuring effects, audit actual functional dependencies and record the exact module path, output boundary, invocation index, tensor layout, masks and cropping. Patch the complete vector after the selected residual addition and masking, before the next block; adapt the hook to the actual implementation rather than assuming a particular output layout. For width-k dilation-d causal convolutions, offsets are {0,d,...,(k-1)d}; serial paths take Minkowski sums and parallel/residual paths take unions. Pointwise operations preserve positions. Include both gate and value dependencies in input-dependent products and include gate pooling or other global paths. A structural span alone is insufficient. If functional paths cannot be established, return an explicit unavailable result rather than claiming locality.

Choose the intermediate boundary after block floor(B/2)-1 for B residual blocks, requiring B>=2. Using audited upstream offsets U and downstream offsets D, enumerate earlier occupied positions p such that r-p is in D and p-i is in U for some occupied positive-lag input i, where r is the original readout. Choose the largest such p, independent of scores, targets and patch outcomes. For each realized corruption, record whether any actually changed input reaches p. Report effects both across all scheduled corruptions and within the structurally reachable subset; this subset is selected by graph and input changes, not score response. If no position satisfies the rule, record an eligibility exclusion. Structural reachability permits an effect but does not guarantee one.

Capture detached clones of clean and corrupted boundary outputs and verify expected hook invocation counts, shapes, dtype, finite values and cache integrity. Patch only the selected recipient position with the donor’s complete hidden vector. Run clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption using the same frozen network and compare each with its own recipient baseline. Identity patches must reproduce final features and candidate scores within disclosed FP32 tolerances, initially atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5. Record actual differences and failures. Verify replacement values inside the hook. A deliberately altered vector must change the intended intermediate tensor; it need not change downstream scores, since downstream insensitivity is possible. Failed execution, layout, identity or replacement checks invalidate the affected site; an incomplete optional control is reported separately.

For the first two eligible users/category, selected without scores, use their first nonidentity permutation for additional controls. Patch the coherent occupied intermediate window [max(0,r-max(D)),r] intersected with occupied positions, and patch the entire intermediate output tensor. The window is a contiguous superset of downstream-reachable positions; disclose extra positions included. Whole-layer restoration should reproduce the donor’s downstream outputs only if all suffix inputs and bypass paths are captured at that boundary. Audit this condition before calling it a restoration control; otherwise mark it unavailable. Where an occupied position cannot reach r, run an unreachable-site negative control; if no such position exists, mark it unavailable. Compare local versus window effects descriptively. These two users cannot support population claims about distributed mediation. Defer factorial patches, complementary ablations and additional independent-donor experiments to a later prespecified study.

Retain bounded repeatability, batch-consistency, readout-agreement, future-invariance and padding checks, documenting their limited scope. Compare actual diagnostic and deployed scores using identical checkpoint, route, IDs, padding, truncation, masking, readout and score transformation when the deployed predictor is accessible. If export parity is unavailable, state this explicitly and confine claims to the ModelView execution path. Compare downstream norms and distances with recorded natural-state references where available; support flags can identify unusual hybrid states but cannot certify distributional support or mechanistic faithfulness.

Do not gate patch execution on clean-corrupted score changes. Report clean-corrupted score-vector L-infinity distance and gap distributions. For compatibility with the existing staged analysis, optionally report a descriptive responsive subset using G=1 when any candidate-score difference exceeds 1e-6+1e-5*abs(clean score), plus thresholds multiplied by 0.1 and 10. Report E[Delta], E[Delta|G=1], gate counts and coverage separately. Because every scheduled eligible corruption is patched, the unconditional mean remains measured. If runtime leaves nongated examples unpatched, mark that unconditional estimand missing; assigning zero would instead measure a different gated intervention policy. Numerical tolerances are proposed protocol defaults, not scientifically established sensitivity thresholds.

Average corruption draws within each user before equal-user aggregation. Report all/repeat-target/novel-target summaries and exploration/confirmation results separately. For responsive subsets, disclose whether the estimand averages eligible draws within each responsive user, and report responsive draw and user counts; never silently reweight users by their number of responsive draws. Use 2,000 paired user-bootstrap replicates with seed 42 and percentile 95% intervals only with at least ten contributing users. Resample complete user records, preserving candidates, corruptions, conditions and gate indicators; recompute all subset denominators. Report undefined empty-subset replicates. Eight confirmation users yield descriptive effects without bootstrap intervals under this rule. Intervals condition on selected users, checkpoint, diagnostic candidates and realized draws; they exclude training-seed, candidate-draw and adaptive-search uncertainty. A separate aggregator may resample users independently within each category and recompute equal-weight four-category diagnostic means only when all four categories expose compatible measurements. Never label these as validation intervals.

Use an explicit 120-second synchronized execution budget/category, covering measured GPU work and CPU diagnostic processing, with at most 32 users, three permutations, one main site and two control users. A main event requires two clean forwards per user for baseline/identity checks and four forwards per corruption for corrupted baseline, corrupted identity, restoration and disruption: at most 448 main forwards/category. Additional controls and parity checks have a separate cap of 32 forwards, giving at most 480 total; catalog scoring is deferred. Batch compatible conditions when supported and bound cached activation memory. Synchronize CUDA before timing boundaries; check remaining budget before each complete condition bundle and report overshoot from any in-flight bundle. Avoid retaining partially completed pairs in paired estimates. Report scheduled/completed users, draws, forwards, runtime, missing controls and truncation order. Timeout-completed users can be a selected subset; full scheduled-cohort effects remain unavailable if incomplete. All work consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

No training or deployed inference change is required for this diagnostic. Preserve all four routes, exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch and single-GPU execution. Do not average checkpoints, fit auxiliary predictors, fuse independent scores or reuse other trials. Any later architecture change must update the embedded predictor writer consistently. Keep pinned host macro validation HR@10 as the sole model-selection criterion; never reconstruct unavailable host candidates or inspect hidden test data. The diagnostic does not establish intent, ownership, satisfaction, compatibility, generalization or validation gains. Save a trial-local replay manifest containing protocol version, checkpoint identity, user/event selection, candidates, permutations, site metadata, controls, tolerances, counts and execution status.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    saved = save_all_module_modes_backends_and_rng(view.model)
    hooks = []
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            timer = synchronized_budget(seconds=120)
            events = cache_and_uniquely_match_training_events(
                train_loader, max_batches=10, max_users=32, seed=42,
                selection_independent_of_scores=True)
            exploration, confirmation = fixed_user_split(events, last_n=8)
            graph = audit_actual_functional_dependency_sets(view.model)
            boundary = boundary_after_block(len(graph.blocks) // 2 - 1)
            if not valid_intermediate_boundary(boundary, graph):
                return metrics_and_definitions_with_missing_reason()
            parity = compare_deployed_scores_if_accessible()
            for event in events:
                r = maximum_nonzero_index(event.sequence)
                candidates = freeze_or_construct_diagnostic_candidates(
                    event, max_unique_negatives=99, seed=42,
                    retain_repeat_target=True)
                p = largest_eligible_earlier_position(event, boundary, graph, r)
                if p is None:
                    record_eligibility_exclusion()
                    continue
                if not budget_allows_complete_bundle(timer):
                    record_timeout_and_uncompleted_schedule()
                    break
                clean = forward_capture(event.sequence, boundary, r, candidates)
                clean_self = patch_forward(event.sequence, boundary,
                    clone(clean.activation), positions=[p], readout=r,
                    candidates=candidates)
                require_execution_and_identity_controls(clean, clean_self)
                for perm in three_recorded_endpoint_preserving_permutations(event):
                    if not budget_allows_complete_bundle(timer):
                        record_incomplete_user_and_remaining_draws()
                        break
                    corrupted = forward_capture(perm.sequence, boundary, r, candidates)
                    corrupted_self = patch_forward(perm.sequence, boundary,
                        clone(corrupted.activation), positions=[p],
                        readout=r, candidates=candidates)
                    require_execution_and_identity_controls(corrupted, corrupted_self)
                    restored = patch_forward(perm.sequence, boundary,
                        clone(clean.activation), positions=[p],
                        readout=r, candidates=candidates)
                    disrupted = patch_forward(event.sequence, boundary,
                        clone(corrupted.activation), positions=[p],
                        readout=r, candidates=candidates)
                    record_complete_pair(
                        restoration=outcomes(restored)-outcomes(corrupted),
                        disruption=outcomes(disrupted)-outcomes(clean),
                        corruption_gap=outcomes(clean)-outcomes(corrupted),
                        changed_inputs_reach_site=graph.reaches(perm.changed, p),
                        score_responsiveness=descriptive_gates(clean, corrupted))
                run_prespecified_extra_controls_if_selected_and_budgeted(
                    event, max_control_users=2, extra_forward_cap=32)
            summaries = equal_user_summaries_of_complete_scheduled_draws()
            intervals = paired_user_bootstrap(
                summaries, replicates=2000, seed=42, minimum_users=10,
                recompute_subset_denominators=True)
            save_trial_local_replay_manifest()
            return {'metrics': measured_results_counts_errors_and_missing_reasons(),
                    'metric_definitions': formulas_protocol_scope_and_estimands()}
    finally:
        remove_all_temporary_hooks(hooks)
        restore_all_module_modes_backends_and_rng(saved)

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embeds both returned dictionaries.
# Require evidence-linked findings, separate missing evidence from null effects,
# and prohibit interpreting intervention effects as user intent or validation gains.

originality.positive: Combines endpoint-preserving corruption, exact temporal dependency rules and bidirectional full-vector interventions in the supplied NextItNet diagnostic.
originality.negative: The methods and controls are established; the contribution is a reproducible family-specific integration rather than a new causal-identification method.

future_potential.positive: Can provide a disciplined foundation for studies of distributed temporal mediation and subsequent controlled single-model training experiments.
future_potential.negative: Conditional patch effects may not transfer across users, corruption protocols or checkpoints, and do not predict improvements in pinned validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing caches, scoring interfaces, hooks and aggregation reduce implementation work, and no retraining or deployment modification is required.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact graph auditing, reliable boundary hooks, coherent-window controls, scoring parity, timeout accounting and reproducible estimands justify increasing the previous difficulty rating.

related_work.title: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces NextItNet’s residual causal dilated convolutional architecture for sequential recommendation.
Provides architectural coordinates for interventions across residual depth and temporal position.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed activation-patching diagnostic.
Exact dependency propagation must follow the actual implementation, including gates, masking, cropping and normalization; the paper alone cannot certify the supplied model.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption methods, measurement choices and patching windows affect localization conclusions.
Supports explicit corruption protocols, raw score-difference measurements and window comparisons.
limitations: Language-model findings do not validate a recommendation-specific protocol.
Endpoint-preserving permutations remain potentially unrealistic counterfactuals.
Controlled patch effects do not identify a unique feature or establish validation benefit.

related_work.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
contributions: Makelov, Lange, Geiger and Nanda demonstrate that successful subspace interventions can activate dormant pathways instead of identifying naturally used features.
Motivates caution when treating intervention success as evidence of a faithful mechanism.
limitations: Corrects the previously supplied paper title.
Projection-induced subspace illusions do not establish that full-vector residual-state replacement has the same failure mechanism.
Full-vector patches still create hybrid states; identity and distance controls cannot certify their faithfulness.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can alter model comparisons.
Supports reporting candidate protocols and separating diagnostic candidate results from full-catalog claims.
limitations: Does not change the mandated pinned evaluator.
Does not establish which diagnostic candidate distribution captures immediate user needs.
The proposed fixed diagnostic candidates support paired intervention comparisons, not general conclusions about full-catalog recommendation quality.

related_work.title: torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode
contributions: Documents inference-mode execution and its distinction from evaluation mode.
Supports using both model.eval() and inference_mode() for the frozen diagnostic.
limitations: Inference mode does not automatically enable evaluation mode.
Neither setting alone guarantees deterministic execution, correct hooks or deployed scoring parity.

related_work.title: scipy.stats.bootstrap
contributions: Documents paired resampling and confidence-interval procedures.
Provides implementation guidance for preserving matched observations across conditions.
limitations: The resampling unit and estimand must still be specified correctly; this protocol resamples complete user records.
Small conditional user samples do not capture training, candidate-draw or adaptive-search uncertainty.
